rows.describe: concurrent requests
rows.evidence: client_test.exs:447-448 — `assert {:ok, _} = Task.await(t1)` twice. Only the return-tuple SHAPE is asserted; no value on either side of the wire is checked. ESCALATION — this unit's OWN assertions are all SDK-invented values (ET-OUT), but it calls the do_connect/2 helper (client_test.exs:59-80), which contains `assert discover["method"] == "server/discover"` and `assert result.server_info.name == "test-server"`. A test is indivisible, so under §6's any-assertion rule those helper assertions are this test's assertions and would lift it to ET-CC. Labelled ET-OUT here because that is the answer the PM's tie-break (comment 26026) gives for the artefact this unit is ABOUT, and because the alternative makes every test sharing an asserting setup helper an ET-CC member. rows.describe: mint/2 and verify/2 — the accept path
rows.evidence: conformance_request_state_test.exs:40 — `{:ok, ^payload} = verify(key, mint(key, payload))`. The asserted artefact is a fixture-invented result atom/tuple (`{:error, :bad_tag}`, `{:error, :malformed}`, `{:ok, payload}`), which has no wire counterpart at all — nothing named `bad_tag` or `malformed` ever appears in a JSON-RPC message. Gate 2 fails. `MCP.Conformance.RequestState` lives at `conformance/request_state.ex` and is the CONFORMANCE SERVER FIXTURE's helper, not SDK code — the file's own moduledoc says so at :19-21 ("The fixture's helper is a fixture, not the product answer — the SDK offers no mint/verify for requestState"). ET-ADJ is therefore unreachable by construction: §5 requires a call site that is "a `file:line` in `lib/`", and there is none — `grep -rn "RequestState" lib/` returns nothing. This file is the mirror image of HAZARD 4: gate 1 scopes on LOCATION, and this instrument-testing file sits under test/mcp/, so all 12 units are IN the 579 and are excluded at 2 or 3 rather than at 1.

The client's own outbound capabilities at client.ex:825 come from a %ClientCapabilities{} STRUCT built at :969, never from from_map/1. ET-OUT. || PM ruling E (26036) applied, and this is the starkest of the six: schema.ts:95-96 states IN WORDS that an empty ClientCapabilities object means the client supports no optional capabilities, which is exactly what the three nils assert. The wire state is `{}` — present and governed, not merely admissible. GATE 3 APPLIED AND PASSES. falsifiable: undetermined per §4. || MES-81 round 4 (PM correction contract, comments 26058-26060). The boundary is SPLIT BY DIRECTION: a `defimpl Jason.Encoder` and a `from_map/1` are different code running in opposite directions, so one direction's liveness may not carry the other (PM ruling, 26058). This row asserts values the DECODE direction produced, and that direction is recorded DEAD: L1 reddened no unit outside the dead family, the L2 byte probe (conformance/etcc_l2_probe.exs) moved no scenario, and every lib/ call site of the decoder sits inside a module lib/ never uses. rows.evidence: initialize_test.exs:35-38 asserts the decoded InitializeParams — protocol_version "2025-11-25", capabilities.roots.list_changed, client_info.name/version. GATE 3 FAILS — `initialize` is REMOVED at 2026-07-28 (SEP-2575). `grep -n "nitialize" schema.ts` at 5f5440bb returns ZERO hits: there is no InitializeRequest/InitializeParams/InitializeResult type in the pinned schema. The only 2026-07-28 prose mentioning it (versioning.mdx:129-178, stdio.mdx:124-145, streamable-http.mdx:653-664, discover.mdx:78) governs LEGACY-ERA INTEROP — whether a dual-era server answers it at all — and defines none of the fields asserted here. rows.question:
DISCLOSURE-ESCALATION (one question, one answer settles every row carrying this text). The module under test is used NOWHERE in lib/: `grep -rn "Messages.Tools" lib/ conformance/` at 94f4d2a returns 128 lines at THIS tip, of which exactly ONE is lib/ (`lib/mcp/protocol/messages/tools.ex`, its own defmodule) and 127 are this register's own bytes under `conformance/data/` — 123 lines / 160 occurrences in `etcc-decisions.json` plus 4 in `etcc-boundaries.json`. *** ROUND-4 CORRECTION (F7, CODE_REVIEWER at 26056; PM ruled it BLOCKING at 26059 item 5). TWO defects in the sentence this replaces. (a) The stated command `grep -rn "Messages.Tools" lib/ conformance/` NOW SELF-HITS: the register it justifies is itself under `conformance/`, so re-running it as written cannot reproduce "only its own defmodule line". The claim survives on the lib/-only form, re-run at this tip and ALIAS-AWARE — `grep -rnE "\bTools\b" lib/` returns two lines, both doc prose (`types/tool.ex:5`, `client.ex:223`), and zero code references. Same shape as the `state_handle_test` self-hit fixed in round 3, on 37 rows instead of 4. (b) The conjunct "and the same holds for ... Messages.Response" is FALSE and is WITHDRAWN FROM THIS ROW, not merely from the prose — `Response` is aliased at protocol.ex:7, client.ex:98 and connection.ex:35, constructed at protocol.ex:98 and pattern-matched throughout client.ex and connection.ex, every one of them INBOUND. This is the F3 remedy applied to the 36 rows F3 did not reach. The narrower claim that survives, and the only one this label rests on, is that `Response.success/2` and `Response.error/2` have ZERO lib/ call sites (`grep -rnE "Response\.(success|error|new)\(" lib/` returns 0, re-run at this tip). NO LABEL MOVES: `Messages.Tools` is dead either way. See S7-16. *** The SDK builds its own wire messages by hand (dispatch.ex:723-729, plug.ex send_json_error, client.ex:868 encode/1). MY DECISION, and I would defend it: gate 2 PASSES. §2's own words are "the gate is on what is asserted, not on where the test sits", and what is asserted here is a JSON-RPC message member — a wire artefact by §2's first clause. A consumer calling this public encode/decode boundary puts exactly these bytes on the wire. THE FACT THAT COULD OVERTURN IT: §2.1's counterfactual reads "would an SDK that got this wire behaviour arbitrarily wrong still pass this test?", and if "this wire behaviour" means "the message THIS SDK actually emits", the answer is yes — a broken dispatch.ex leaves every one of these green. Disclosed rather than absorbed because it is a fact about the tree, not a judgement, and it moves 45 rows to ET-OUT if the PM reads §2.1 the second way (ET-OUT, not ET-ADJ: with no lib/ call site, ET-ADJ's positive test cannot be met).

ADJUDICATED by PM ruling A (26034): an assertion on the output of a public encode/decode boundary that NO lib/ call site routes to a transport fails gate 2. Established per row at 2026-08-23 by encoder mutation over the full 979-unit suite; see `evidence`.

The module under test is used NOWHERE in lib/: `grep -rn "Messages.Tools" lib/ conformance/` at 94f4d2a returns 128 lines at THIS tip, of which exactly ONE is lib/ (`lib/mcp/protocol/messages/tools.ex`, its own defmodule) and 127 are this register's own bytes under `conformance/data/` — 123 lines / 160 occurrences in `etcc-decisions.json` plus 4 in `etcc-boundaries.json`. *** ROUND-4 CORRECTION (F7, CODE_REVIEWER at 26056; PM ruled it BLOCKING at 26059 item 5). TWO defects in the sentence this replaces. (a) The stated command `grep -rn "Messages.Tools" lib/ conformance/` NOW SELF-HITS: the register it justifies is itself under `conformance/`, so re-running it as written cannot reproduce "only its own defmodule line". The claim survives on the lib/-only form, re-run at this tip and ALIAS-AWARE — `grep -rnE "\bTools\b" lib/` returns two lines, both doc prose (`types/tool.ex:5`, `client.ex:223`), and zero code references. Same shape as the `state_handle_test` self-hit fixed in round 3, on 37 rows instead of 4. (b) The conjunct "and the same holds for ... Messages.Response" is FALSE and is WITHDRAWN FROM THIS ROW, not merely from the prose — `Response` is aliased at protocol.ex:7, client.ex:98 and connection.ex:35, constructed at protocol.ex:98 and pattern-matched throughout client.ex and connection.ex, every one of them INBOUND. This is the F3 remedy applied to the 36 rows F3 did not reach. The narrower claim that survives, and the only one this label rests on, is that `Response.success/2` and `Response.error/2` have ZERO lib/ call sites (`grep -rnE "Response\.(success|error|new)\(" lib/` returns 0, re-run at this tip). NO LABEL MOVES: `Messages.Tools` is dead either way. See S7-16. *** The SDK builds its own wire messages by hand (dispatch.ex:723-729, plug.ex send_json_error, client.ex:868 encode/1). MY DECISION, and I would defend it: gate 2 PASSES. §2's own words are "the gate is on what is asserted, not on where the test sits", and what is asserted here is a JSON-RPC message member — a wire artefact by §2's first clause. A consumer calling this public encode/decode boundary puts exactly these bytes on the wire. THE FACT THAT COULD OVERTURN IT: §2.1's counterfactual reads "would an SDK that got this wire behaviour arbitrarily wrong still pass this test?", and if "this wire behaviour" means "the message THIS SDK actually emits", the answer is yes — a broken dispatch.ex leaves every one of these green. Disclosed rather than absorbed because it is a fact about the tree, not a judgement, and it moves 45 rows to ET-OUT if the PM reads §2.1 the second way (ET-OUT, not ET-ADJ: with no lib/ call site, ET-ADJ's positive test cannot be met).

ADJUDICATED by PM ruling A (26034): an assertion on the output of a public encode/decode boundary that NO lib/ call site routes to a transport fails gate 2. Established per row at 2026-08-23 by encoder mutation over the full 979-unit suite; see `evidence`.

adjudication.outcome: overturned: provisional ET-CC -> ET-OUT, excluding gate 2

rows.describe: CallResult — structuredContent may be any JSON value
rows.evidence: tools_test.exs:147-148 — for `an empty string`: the ENCODED map has the "structuredContent" KEY and its value is `an empty string` unchanged. One of 10 units the `for` at :131 generates, labelled per unit. `false`, `""`, `[]` and `%{}` are the discriminating ones: the old encoder used `if struct.structured_content`, which is falsy on false. Contrast tool_test.exs:109, where a boolean IS ET-OUT because outputSchema is typed as an OBJECT — here the schema enumerates booleans explicitly, which is why one is a member and the other is not. Module unused in lib/ — see the escalation question on this row. || PM ruling A (26034), established per row rather than swept: the encoder that produces the asserted artefact was MUTATED and the whole suite re-run. Mutating `Messages.Tools` (ListParams cursor key, CallResult content/isError keys, the structuredContent encoder key) reddened 18 units, ALL of them MCP.Protocol.Messages.ToolsTest; 0 of the other 961. No unit outside this file's own reddened, so §2.1's counterfactual returns YES and gate 2 fails. §5 way (i): no lib/ call site consumes the artefact on a wire-producing path, so ET-ADJ is unreachable.

rows.question: GATE-3 BOUNDARY, escalated because it decides a family of 7 rows and I can argue it both ways. These units assert an identity STRING that the SDK threaded from ToolContext.identity into a handler and out through a spec-defined response envelope. Gate 2 passes: the artefact read is the decoded server response and the test would raise or fail if `content`/`text`/`messages`/`resourceTemplates` were misspelled. PROVISIONAL: ET-OUT at gate 3, on §10 category 6 — 'reaches the wire, but the spec does not govern the value being exercised. The one that looks most like a member and is not.' No 2026-07-28 requirement governs what a tool returns, nor says that a model-supplied `identity` argument must not become the caller principal; that rule is CLAUDE.md critical rule 6, sourced from this project's identity-threading design spec, not from the pinned revision. The nearest spec text is schema.ts:85-88 (clientInfo 'is not verified by the protocol', servers 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'), which is about clientInfo in _meta and not about tool arguments — naming it would be the AC7 error of claiming a bound that does not hold. THE OTHER READING: the envelope field names ARE load-bearing for whether these tests pass, and §3 only requires that the sweeper can PRODUCE an anchor — CallToolResult.content (schema.ts:1813), TextContent.text (:2316-2320), GetPromptResult.messages, ListResourceTemplatesResult.resourceTemplates (:1169-1171) are all nameable. On that reading every one of these is ET-CC with mixed: true. I take the first reading because §12's second inherited warning says a proxy for a gate is not the gate, and the envelope is how the value travelled rather than what the unit claims.

adjudication.outcome: upheld as ruled: gate 3 fails on §10 category 6; no change

rows.question: GATE-3 BOUNDARY, escalated because it decides a family of 7 rows and I can argue it both ways. These units assert an identity STRING that the SDK threaded from ToolContext.identity into a handler and out through a spec-defined response envelope. Gate 2 passes: the artefact read is the decoded server response and the test would raise or fail if `content`/`text`/`messages`/`resourceTemplates` were misspelled. PROVISIONAL: ET-OUT at gate 3, on §10 category 6 — 'reaches the wire, but the spec does not govern the value being exercised. The one that looks most like a member and is not.' No 2026-07-28 requirement governs what a tool returns, nor says that a model-supplied `identity` argument must not become the caller principal; that rule is CLAUDE.md critical rule 6, sourced from this project's identity-threading design spec, not from the pinned revision. The nearest spec text is schema.ts:85-88 (clientInfo 'is not verified by the protocol', servers 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'), which is about clientInfo in _meta and not about tool arguments — naming it would be the AC7 error of claiming a bound that does not hold. THE OTHER READING: the envelope field names ARE load-bearing for whether these tests pass, and §3 only requires that the sweeper can PRODUCE an anchor — CallToolResult.content (schema.ts:1813), TextContent.text (:2316-2320), GetPromptResult.messages, ListResourceTemplatesResult.resourceTemplates (:1169-1171) are all nameable. On that reading every one of these is ET-CC with mixed: true. I take the first reading because §12's second inherited warning says a proxy for a gate is not the gate, and the envelope is how the value travelled rather than what the unit claims.

rows.question: GATE-3 BOUNDARY, escalated because it decides a family of 7 rows and I can argue it both ways. These units assert an identity STRING that the SDK threaded from ToolContext.identity into a handler and out through a spec-defined response envelope. Gate 2 passes: the artefact read is the decoded server response and the test would raise or fail if `content`/`text`/`messages`/`resourceTemplates` were misspelled. PROVISIONAL: ET-OUT at gate 3, on §10 category 6 — 'reaches the wire, but the spec does not govern the value being exercised. The one that looks most like a member and is not.' No 2026-07-28 requirement governs what a tool returns, nor says that a model-supplied `identity` argument must not become the caller principal; that rule is CLAUDE.md critical rule 6, sourced from this project's identity-threading design spec, not from the pinned revision. The nearest spec text is schema.ts:85-88 (clientInfo 'is not verified by the protocol', servers 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'), which is about clientInfo in _meta and not about tool arguments — naming it would be the AC7 error of claiming a bound that does not hold. THE OTHER READING: the envelope field names ARE load-bearing for whether these tests pass, and §3 only requires that the sweeper can PRODUCE an anchor — CallToolResult.content (schema.ts:1813), TextContent.text (:2316-2320), GetPromptResult.messages, ListResourceTemplatesResult.resourceTemplates (:1169-1171) are all nameable. On that reading every one of these is ET-CC with mixed: true. I take the first reading because §12's second inherited warning says a proxy for a gate is not the gate, and the envelope is how the value travelled rather than what the unit claims.

The nearest spec text is schema.ts:85-88 (clientInfo 'is not verified by the protocol', servers 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'), which is about clientInfo in _meta and not about tool arguments — naming it would be the AC7 error of claiming a bound that does not hold. THE OTHER READING: the envelope field names ARE load-bearing for whether these tests pass, and §3 only requires that the sweeper can PRODUCE an anchor — CallToolResult.content (schema.ts:1813), TextContent.text (:2316-2320), GetPromptResult.messages, ListResourceTemplatesResult.resourceTemplates (:1169-1171) are all nameable. On that reading every one of these is ET-CC with mixed: true. I take the first reading because §12's second inherited warning says a proxy for a gate is not the gate, and the envelope is how the value travelled rather than what the unit claims.

rows.question: GATE-3 BOUNDARY, escalated because it decides a family of 7 rows and I can argue it both ways. These units assert an identity STRING that the SDK threaded from ToolContext.identity into a handler and out through a spec-defined response envelope. Gate 2 passes: the artefact read is the decoded server response and the test would raise or fail if `content`/`text`/`messages`/`resourceTemplates` were misspelled. PROVISIONAL: ET-OUT at gate 3, on §10 category 6 — 'reaches the wire, but the spec does not govern the value being exercised. The one that looks most like a member and is not.' No 2026-07-28 requirement governs what a tool returns, nor says that a model-supplied `identity` argument must not become the caller principal; that rule is CLAUDE.md critical rule 6, sourced from this project's identity-threading design spec, not from the pinned revision. The nearest spec text is schema.ts:85-88 (clientInfo 'is not verified by the protocol', servers 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'), which is about clientInfo in _meta and not about tool arguments — naming it would be the AC7 error of claiming a bound that does not hold. THE OTHER READING: the envelope field names ARE load-bearing for whether these tests pass, and §3 only requires that the sweeper can PRODUCE an anchor — CallToolResult.content (schema.ts:1813), TextContent.text (:2316-2320), GetPromptResult.messages, ListResourceTemplatesResult.resourceTemplates (:1169-1171) are all nameable. On that reading every one of these is ET-CC with mixed: true. I take the first reading because §12's second inherited warning says a proxy for a gate is not the gate, and the envelope is how the value travelled rather than what the unit claims.

rows.evidence: streamable_http_client_test.exs:112-113 — `content-encoding: identity` is tolerated: `:ok` and the decoded message is delivered to the owner. GATE 2 PASSES on the second assertion — `assert_receive {:mcp_message, %{"result" => %{"ok" => true}}}` reads a decoded JSON-RPC response that crossed a real HTTP connection. GATE 3 FAILS, established by search rather than assumed: `grep -rn "ccept-[Ee]ncoding\|ontent-[Ee]ncoding\|gzip"` over the whole pinned docs/specification/2026-07-28 tree and schema.ts returns ZERO hits. Content coding is governed by RFC 9110 §12.5.3 (a SHOULD) and the SDK's choice here is a security decision against EEF-CVE-2026-49755 (req's decompression is opt-in and unbounded — a decompression-bomb DoS), not an MCP requirement. §10 category 6. The `%{"ok" => true}` body is a ProbePlug fixture, and the claim the unit makes is about content-coding tolerance, which nothing in the pinned revision governs.

rows.evidence: transport_test.exs:20-23 — hand-written maps are pushed through `MockTransport.send_message/2` and read back out of `sent_messages/1`. Nothing here is produced by the SDK: the "method" => "ping" value is the TEST's own literal, so gate 2 fails (no wire artefact of ours is asserted) and gate 3 fails (no requirement governs our test double). It is APPARATUS in §5.3's sense — `test/support/mock_transport.ex` is not lib/ and ships in no release — and roughly 90 in-scope units read their wire evidence out of `sent_messages/1`; if it silently recorded nothing, every one of them would pass vacuously. controls names one such unit (client_test.exs:182).
